entries.about: the storm comes toward her like an angry dog; ice rain like bees, then unease and loneliness, the sky pressing in to smother her. plain storm writing, cut off mid-sentence.
entries.quote: it is like i am standing on the edge of an abyss.
entries.text:
maybe someone is pulling it to find out what lies beneath.

the wind tells me all its secrets and then laughs. i hear thunder rumble, like an angry dog. it is coming towards me.

my mind has been on other things today, i do not notice the rain until it touches me, like tiny ice crystals falling, stinging me like bees. when it hits me, i feel the shock of it.

it falls harder, then, like a hundred icy fingers stroking me at the same time. i begin to shiver and it becomes cold. i am aware of a growing sense of unease, and of loneliness. it is like i am standing on the edge of an abyss. the clouds gather closer and the sky seems to press in, as if trying to smother me. suddenly there are lightning and thunder.

entries.about: someone hiding in her hair pulls it to make her look behind her; the storm's power in her blood, the house groaning like a giant, and 'we' are pulled up above the clouds.
entries.quote: the house groans like a giant, settling itself for the night.
entries.text:
maybe someone is hiding in it. they pull my hair to make me stop walking and look behind me.

when the storm hits i feel the power of it in my blood. the winds make the windows shake, and the house groans like a giant, settling itself for the night. lightning strikes the tall towers of the town, the electricity fizzing like soda through the wires. my heart is beating fast in my chest as we are pulled by some great power towards the doors and up into the sky, above the clouds. it feels like a storm that has come and gone.

entries.about: hail on the roof; up there it is easy to be happy and her tears fall straight down instead of falling upwards like rain. the birds sing la la la and she doesn't know why.
entries.quote: and the birds sing ‘la, la, la.’ i don’t know why.
entries.text:
pulling my head backwards, until i feel dizzy. so i run my fingers through it until my nails catch in it.

when i am on top of the house, it is easy to be happy. it is all so clear, even the stars, though they are further away than usual. and my tears can fall directly to the earth, instead of falling upwards and falling again and again like the rain.

and then it begins to hail, but the ice balls just bounce off of my head and the birds sing ‘la, la, la.’ i don’t know why.

entries.about: a party in a castle, a knight who lives in a tower and moves into the bathroom — then the narrator steps out to say this is the best joke in the world. the joke direction arrives.
entries.quote: I never get tired of this joke. It’s so stupid, but I love it so much.
entries.text:
sometimes when the moon is high in the sky i let my hair down to wash it. after ten minutes i go back upstairs because my room is wet.

once i was at a party in a castle and the fire went out. the knight who lives in the castle said he didn’t mind. it’s okay, he said, I live in a tower. He still wasn’t happy with his life so he moved into the bathroom.

I never get tired of this joke. It’s so stupid, but I love it so much. It’s the best joke in the world. I can’t help but tell it to people and ruin their day, just so I can see them laugh. They say it’s the oldest joke in the world and I think that’s a good sign because it’s probably been going round forever and making people laugh just as

entries.about: 30 words, deadpan: the rain comes down like rain, not this time; her body flies across the field into the lake, and it's dead. an anti-joke in the storm-girl's voice.
entries.quote: sometimes when it rains, it comes down like rain. but not this time.
entries.text:
sometimes when it rains, it comes down like rain. but not this time.

the wind blows again. my body goes flying across the field, into the lake. and it's dead.

entries.about: 41 words: her hair pulls her down to the earth, and there are many eyes watching from the trees, the rocks, the hollow trunks; she can't see them all at once.
entries.quote: i cannot see them all at once. but i know they’re there.
entries.text:
pulling my head backwards, down to the earth.

and there are many eyes watching from between the branches of trees, from behind rocks and from the hollowed out trunks. i cannot see them all at once. but i know they’re there.

entries.about: 'they' tell her not to look at the ground, to fear thunder, not to cry for the moon; the sun turns her into an owl; she can't stop talking and they want her to stop.
entries.quote: they tell me to be afraid of thunder. and not to cry for the moon.
entries.text:
pulling my head down. but i won’t look at the ground, no matter how many times they tell me to.

they tell me to be afraid of thunder. and not to cry for the moon.

so i look to the sun instead, and it burns bright in my eyes and turns me into an owl. i watch the world change, turn around and become different. i don’t mind. i see you too, sometimes.

i try to explain, and sometimes i succeed. i talk in circles, talk with my hands, talk like a windmill, like a wild cat, like a woman. but it’s all wrong, it’s all wrong. they want me to stop talking. but i can’t stop talking.

i tell them to take it, to take everything and go away. and maybe then they’ll let me alone.

entries.about: the storm pulls her outward; white faces with holes in their cheeks all around; from above she sees her childhood and the empty years after, and the darkness is a blanket she could pull over herself.
entries.quote: i could pull it up over me. and never have to get up again.
entries.text:
pulling me outwards. i look back down from the sky to the ground below and all around me are faces, white faces with holes in their cheeks.

when i am here, high up, i see it all. the fields, the road, the woods beyond. i see my childhood. and all those years after it, the ones with nothing but empty promises. i feel as if i can touch them. when i close my eyes and let my hand float towards the darkness i am standing in i can almost reach them. it feels like a heavy blanket. i could pull it up over me. and never have to get up again.

entries.about: a fever where the sheets were earth, sky and sea; her father says they are all children of god — and she says his words will come back to slap him.
entries.quote: it will be us that have to carry this world when it all falls apart.
entries.text:
tugging. tearing. i look down into my heart to see if i’m broken and bleeding.

once i had a fever so hot and I lay on my bed. and the sheets were the colour of the earth, the sky, and the sea, but when I closed my eyes there was an orange sunset and an endless field. there was nothing but space between me and the stars and i was happy.

one night in summer there is a full moon, and my father tells us that we are all the children of god. that our bodies are perfect just the way they are, and he shows us the sky, and he tells us to go play and not worry. but one day his words will come back and slap him hard, because it will be us that have to carry this world when it all falls apart.

the next morning we will

entries.about: 'dragging me out into the night'; lost in the storm and the tales, voices on the edge of her mind whispering flattery.
entries.quote: ‘I’ll be your goddess.’
entries.text:
dragging me out into the night. there’s nothing for it but to run away and cut loose.

once i was lost in it all, the storm and the wind, the torches and the tales. it’s an old story, isn’t it? But still. It’s true what they say: sometimes i think i can hear them, whispering to each other on the edge of my mind.

‘You’re so beautiful,’

‘I’ll be your goddess.’

‘Your skin shines like a jewel.’

entries.about: the storm is a dark hand with a torch and tells her there is no death; she goes down and waits by the window for her mother to call her for tea.
entries.quote: ‘there is no death,’ it tells me, and its words fall like rain onto the earth.
entries.text:
sometimes when the moon is high in the sky i look up and i see stars through it.

when i sleep, i wrap myself around the world.

the storm says to me, ‘do not fear.’ the storm is a dark hand holding a torch, waving back and forth.

‘there is no death,’ it tells me, and its words fall like rain onto the earth.

and so i go back down the stairs. i sit in the house by the window with the curtain drawn. i am waiting for my mother to call me for tea, or maybe to take a nap.

entries.about: someone tugs her hair and laughs out of sight; little hidden things in the undergrowth; she'll whisper her secrets if you come near.
entries.quote: if you come near enough, i will whisper all my secrets, and then, perhaps, you too will find them.
entries.text:
like someone is tugging on it and laughing when i cannot see them. like i am tied down with knots, but then when i look, there are always little things in the undergrowth, hidden away: snails, birds, worms, tiny toads.

if you come near enough, i will whisper all my secrets, and then, perhaps, you too will find them.

entries.about: gravity pulling her back into her skin; everyone lives in an eternal dream; lies, secrets, everyone laughing.
entries.quote: like gravity, pulling me back into my skin.
entries.text:
like gravity, pulling me back into my skin.

all are aware, we live in this eternal dream.

that is how they stay alive, in our dreams.

so it is a shame that the world does can't be so easy, full of lies, secrets...

all these stories that nobody ever heard.

lies. all lies, and everyone is laughing.

so yes, you know, no one is afraid to fall...

all fools, just like them, so foolish to hide...

entries.about: she once broke a glass table with her head and her face split like a snake's; she catches thunder in her teeth; when tired she lets her hair fall into the clouds and the stars hold it.
entries.quote: when i am tired, i let my hair fall into the clouds and the stars hold it up in their hands
entries.text:
pulling my head backwards, away from my shoulders.

it has been this way ever since i fell down and broke the glass table with my head, my mouth full of shards, blood like a river down my neck, the skin of my face split in half like a snake’s.

sometimes the wind brings rain. i wait for the lightning, watch it travel across the sky and try to catch the thunder as it rolls between my teeth, over the backs of my knees. when i am tired, i let my hair fall into the clouds and the stars hold it up in their hands, let it lie on their skin and rest against their bodies, until i am ready to carry it again.

this time the wind carries snowflakes, small and round. i have not seen snowflakes before, i wonder why they are not falling onto the

entries.about: rain makes her a sea witch; the sky has a mouth like a gate; she is not the girl in the story but the storyteller — then a saint augustine quote as a tail.
entries.quote: i am not the girl in the story, but the storyteller
entries.text:
sometimes when the rain pours down it sticks to my face and i look like the sea witch from the stories, all wrinkles and deep creases and salt and wind. the sky has a mouth like a tunnel, a passage, like a gate, like an archway to another world. and we whisper through it.

i am always the girl with the windswept hair. i am the girl who runs away to find adventure, or the girl who goes searching for answers to her questions, or the girl who dreams of something greater.

i am not the girl in the story, but the storyteller, the one who looks at the sky and tells herself that she will find what she’s looking for someday soon.

the world is a book, and those who do not travel read only a page – saint augustine

entries.about: at night spiders and moths live in her hair; her eyes search the earth for faces of relatives she never met and knows only as voices.
entries.quote: i have heard stories about them, but i have no face to go with those names
entries.text:
sometimes when the rain pours down it sticks to my face and i look like an animal that has fallen into a puddle.

when the sun sets and it becomes night, the darkness comes, and all of the little things start to crawl. spiders spin webs in my hair. moths get stuck inside and try to get out again, beating their wings against my cheeks and forehead. tiny little bugs fly into my eyes and crawl in my mouth.

i look around to see what i have been missing, who i might have known but never met. my eyes are like searchlights, they scour the earth, they find faces. i have never met my grandmother, my uncle, my sister. i have heard stories about them, but i have no face to go with those names, only their voices echoing inside my head.

when it

entries.about: like being underwater, stars in her skin; her hair sinks her into an underground river older than time — then a history: the Picts of Orkney, a woman stolen while bathing.
entries.quote: down into an underground river which has been there since time began.
entries.text:
pulling my head backwards, down into the dirt.

it’s like I’m underwater. The sky is black but the trees are orange with their own fire and my skin is full of stars. the rain falls on me. the leaves and stones in my hair absorb them. my hair weighs so much it sinks me into the water, where the reeds reach out for me and pull me down into the mud.

it takes me down into a deep, dark place. down into an underground river which has been there since time began. and here is a story i have heard: In a time long before my time, a people called the Picts lived on the islands of Orkney. One day a woman was bathing naked by the water when a group of men from a foreign tribe came to steal her. They stole her away, taking her back

entries.about: someone fallen in the dirt with blood in their hair; 'we watch the world burn, together' — then the page becomes a news column on Trump.
entries.quote: we watch the world burn, together.
entries.text:
tugging. tearing. i look back down at the ground and i see someone who has fallen into the dirt, their legs twisted beneath them, their hair wet with blood. the rain pours down over us.

it is so hard to know where the storm begins. but we both remember the end of it.

we watch the world burn, together.

### *

“No more ‘threat of terror’, no more ‘security’. I want a police state in this country.”

That was Donald Trump on 6 September, after the terrorist attack in Charlottesville. In his own way, he was just saying the same thing he’s been saying since he began campaigning for president: “I want to be unpredictable”. But then, his words were only the most recent in an increasing number of dog-whistle threats made by western politicians.

entries.about: rain like pins and needles, a thousand whispered secrets; thunder the voice of her god, lightning its smile; after, the quiet river and the world asleep.
entries.quote: the thunder is the voice of my god and the lightening is its smile.
entries.text:
pulling my head backwards, away from my shoulders.

it has been so long since i cut my hair.

when the rain falls it feels like a shower of pins and needles. and when it is heavy it is as if a thousand people are all whispering secrets into my ears.

the thunder is the voice of my god and the lightening is its smile. when it strikes it makes me gasp for breath. my heart pounds against the ribcage, i cannot stop shaking.

and after, there is quiet. there is no noise but the sound of the river. it is a wide and empty place and the world is asleep.

entries.about: people say they love her but never say the word, so she puts herself into the forest and lets roots grow into her hair; she talks to the trees and their leaves change colour.
entries.quote: and let the roots grow into my hair and become part of me, because no one else has ever loved me.
entries.text:
pulling my head backwards, down into the dirt.

and there are people who pull at me too. they tell me they love me but i do not believe them. i will not believe them, because they have never said the word. they do not know how to say it. so instead, i put myself into this forest, and let the roots grow into my hair and become part of me, because no one else has ever loved me.

i tell the trees everything. they hear me speak, but i never hear them answer. instead, the rain falls in big fat drops. the river swells, and the wind comes sweeping over the field and makes the wheat dance.

the trees listen to me. and sometimes when i talk, their leaves change colour.

entries.about: a man with dark blue eyes takes her hand; they watch the sky fall and a voice says she is a woman of great power.
entries.quote: and there is a voice saying: “and you are a woman of great power…”
entries.text:
pulling my body backwards. but i stand tall with my hair like a crown upon my head.

when i hear a noise behind me i turn, my hair flying out in the wind.

and the storm falls.

“and the rain will wash you clean, like snow” he says.

his eyes are deep pools of dark blue, and they are alive.

and then he reaches up to take my hand and together we watch the sky fall, as the clouds part to reveal the sky behind. it is white, like new cotton. and there is a voice saying: “and you are a woman of great power…”

entries.about: icicles become the army of heaven; the voice of God says get ready, it is time to change — a prophetic word.
entries.quote: “get ready, it is time to change!”
entries.text:
sometimes when the rain comes and it falls heavy upon me, it will become soaked and then freeze into icicles, like needles hanging down to the floor. they are like little spears in the hands of an army. the army of heaven, they are angels who sing with their swords drawn. and their swords are made from the water from the heavens and from the sea. their voices come like a rushing river, carrying with them life, breath, healing, deliverance. they carry the breath of God, his presence.

the voice of God is like the sound of the wind, a whisper. he is saying, “get ready, it is time to change!” he says, “you have been prepared, equipped for this moment! You are not just being called, you have been sent!” The call has gone out over the earth; it

entries.about: her fingers in the tangle, scalp hurting; the wind tells her to look at the sky, and it is full of stars.
entries.quote: it says: look at the sky. it has so much light, even in this dark hour.
entries.text:
tugging. tearing. i run my fingers through it to try to free myself and my scalp hurts from all the strain.

some nights the wind speaks to me. it says: look at the sky. it has so much light, even in this dark hour.

and when i look up, it is full of stars.

*

entries.about: clouds full of stars whisper; small creatures laugh in the shadows; from the storm she looks down at the city and thinks maybe someone down there — a child, a baker — is looking too.
entries.quote: and for one moment, just for one fleeting moment, i think that maybe someone down there
entries.text:
sometimes when the clouds are full of stars they whisper to me in the dark.

the trees rustle under my feet. there are secrets there, deep within their branches, that i never find, no matter how many years i search. sometimes, if the moon is high and full of honey, and i listen hard enough, i can hear the laughter of small creatures as they hide from me in the shadows.

and every now and again, if the sky is full of rain and lightning, if the trees are singing and i am running wild with the wind in my hair, i look out over the fields, down to the city lights. and for one moment, just for one fleeting moment, i think that maybe someone down there, maybe a child in the school yard, maybe the baker on his way home from work, maybe even the

entries.about: she and the clouds dance and sing; her mother at the edge of the field says stop, you will upset your father; the sky stills — and she lifts her arms and says she wants to stay.
entries.quote: “stop it,” she says. “you will upset your father.”
entries.text:
sometimes when the clouds are full of stars they whisper to me in the dark.

but there are things you cannot do with clouds.

there is a wind that moves like a wave, like the water when i am alone. the trees are dancing, and the clouds move with me and we dance too, all together. we laugh, and sing, and throw our voices over the mountain and through the trees.

my mother stands at the edge of the field and she looks down on us.

“stop it,” she says. “you will upset your father.”

the wind slows. the leaves fall to the ground. the sky stills. and the clouds grow heavy with rain.

but we keep moving. and i lift my arms up, up, as high as the sun, higher than the moon, and say,

“I want to stay.”

entries.about: clouds carry sorrow and it turns out to be gold; she is a small ship, a little light; 'he' knows her heart.
entries.quote: i am just a small ship, just a little light.
entries.text:
sometimes when the clouds are far away from home they look like they are carrying great loads of sorrow on their backs, but then when they return, they tell me their secret. the burden is a bundle of gold and silver, all the riches in the world.

sometimes it gets cold and lonely. and we curl into each other, the mountains, and i feel like i am standing on an island, just me. there is nothing around, no one else, i could just sit here and watch the storm, alone and afraid. it feels like a great ocean. i am just a small ship, just a little light. and sometimes the wind is too strong. but he knows my heart.

entries.quote: and the stars will take care of my feet. they will always lead me home.
entries.text:
pulling my head backwards, down into the dirt.

and when it is dark enough to see stars in the sky, i sit down on the rooftop and count them. the lights from the buildings below me turn to sparks, falling to the ground like meteors. my feet get cold. i blow my breath across the soles, watching it spread across the concrete like mist.

then, when i am warm again, i can feel the sky. and when it rains i know how to move, how to dance on the tiles and be light like a leaf. i can be water, i can run in between the bricks. and the stars will take care of my feet. they will always lead me home.

entries.about: gravity reaching up with long fingers; she reasons about the sun, the cloud and the one shadow — and asks where the shadow of her hair is.
entries.quote: so, where is the shadow of my hair? where is it, where do you stand? what did the cloud say? am i alone?
entries.text:
pulling my head towards the ground. like gravity has become alive and is reaching up for me with long fingers.

i try not to think about the sun as i move. it is behind the cloud and will only appear when the wind is blowing. if the cloud passes and it appears in front of the sun then i will see a shadow fall. just one.

there are many ways to create shadow, but there is always more than one. so, where is the shadow of my hair? where is it, where do you stand? what did the cloud say? am i alone?

entries.quote: they can carry my name over the horizon, they can give my smile to someone who needs it more.
entries.text:
pulling my head backwards, away from my shoulders.

and there are some days where i want nothing more than to be taken apart by my own body and become nothing but a memory. my heart, my stomach, my blood, my mind – i don’t care anymore. they can go wherever they want to go. my bones, my flesh, they can take whatever they want and do what they will with me. they can carry my name over the horizon, they can give my smile to someone who needs it more.

some days, my skin is so thin. i can feel the world turning. it is like a slow song playing in the back of my mind and i want to lie down and fall asleep. let them pull me out and make a bed for me. i’ll never be warm again, never wake up.

entries.quote: she was too beautiful to look upon, so they took my eyes out when i was a baby, and fed them to dogs. she is my best friend.
entries.text:
sometimes when the moon is high in the sky i let my hair down and dance with it until morning comes.

entries.about: her mother has found the bloody tissue in the bin and left it on the floor for her; it looks like berries; on the roof a 'he' brings her cigarettes. a teenager, frame held.
entries.quote: it looks like berries.
entries.text:
pulling my head backwards, down into the dirt.

and when it is hot i think it smells like smoke.

i try not to cry in the shower but my mother has found the bloody tissue, has taken it from the bin in the bathroom, has left it on the floor so i cannot miss it. now i look at the red stain, feel it under my fingers. i run my thumb over it and then bring it close to my eyes, closer, until my breath stops.

it looks like berries.

the birds sing.

they call to one another. they don’t even have words, but i understand. i don’t need to be told.

entries.about: 55 words: she lets out a howl, a bell; she has lost all sense of self in the storm; it is so loud, this silence.
entries.quote:
it is so loud.

this silence.
entries.text:
pulling my head backwards, down into the dirt.

and then i let out this noise. like an animal or a wild creature. like a howl.

like the sound of a bell.

a storm has come and i have lost all sense of self, lost myself in this wild world.

it is so loud.

this silence.

entries.about: dragged into the forest where three loud voices come and go; a child's register, owls and deer her favourite part.
entries.quote: but there are only three of them and they’re so loud all the time!
entries.text:
like someone is dragging me through the hedges or into the forest. but then it goes away for a bit, and then comes back to me.

the forest is so deep, so dark, but there is so much in there, too, you can hear voices. when you’re hiding in the hedges and they’re not there anymore, they come back again. but there are only three of them and they’re so loud all the time! when the wind blows and they aren’t around, you can really hear them. i’ve never been there before, but i’d go, just to see the trees, and to listen to the owls and the deer. they’re my favourite part of the forest.

entries.about: trees like fingers that bend back to the ground; she feels like one; dry flaky skin, the grass gone brown, the plants wilted.
entries.quote: sometimes i feel like a tree like that.
entries.text:
pulling my head backwards, down to the earth.

and there are these trees that look like fingers reaching into the sky. they’re tall, and wide. they grow from the ground up in a straight line, but at the top, where the branches sprout out, they reach down towards the ground.

sometimes i feel like a tree like that.

my skin has always been dry, flaky, thin. i’ve never understood why, when the trees and plants around me seem so strong and solid. the grass has always looked so healthy to me. its green was so rich, the roots were always so deep, and it swayed in the breeze.

entries.about: a wasting body — muddy rain, stick legs, shoes too big, clouds in her eyes, an empty mind — and she is happy; her hair warm on her back; she sleeps.
entries.quote: my mind is as empty as the space behind my eyes. but i am happy.
entries.text:
sometimes when the rain pours down it drips from my hair in thick strands of muddy water.

when the rain stops i drink it, but my throat is so full of dirt that the rain runs over my lips, over my cheeks, into the folds of my dress. my shoes are too big now. my legs are like sticks, covered in hair that never ends. i think if i tried to take off my shoes they would break. my eyes are dull. there are small clouds in them, little islands that never grow larger or smaller. there is no life there, and my mind is as empty as the space behind my eyes. but i am happy. my hair is thick and soft, and sometimes when i walk, i can feel the sun on my back through it, warm and soft against my shoulders.

i sleep now.

entries.about: her friend says there's no time left, meaning the story she is writing, the story of their life; she wonders about his metaphor; his life in a glass case, named Rav.
entries.quote: and i know he is talking about the story i am writing. the story of our life.
entries.text:
sometimes when the moon is low in the sky i find i have no strength left to walk forward.

then my friend says ‘there’s no time left,’ and i know he is talking about the story i am writing. the story of our life.

i wonder why he chose this particular metaphor. was it because he saw my life in terms of time? or perhaps it was because he saw my life as an empty vessel? did he not see the ocean, the endless blue sky?

it doesn’t matter, because i understand all of those things, i understand that his life was in a glass case. the thing is, he loved that case, he looked after it and cleaned it with love. he called it ‘his muse’, and his name was ‘Rav’ (meaning raven). he was tall and handsome and he loved my father

entries.about: the storm follows her home, its shadow a stain across her bed; other nights lightning, her reflection, the blue lights of a hospital car park, until the pain makes her still.
entries.quote: and the storm follows me home, it’s shadow like a stain on the earth, a thin line across the floor, across my bed.
entries.text:
tugging. twisting. but i let go when it starts to hurt.

sometimes it takes hours for me to get through it all.

and the storm follows me home, it’s shadow like a stain on the earth, a thin line across the floor, across my bed.

but when morning comes, i wake with it still in me and the smell of rain all around.

*

and there are other nights when it comes at me silently, its face hidden, and then i’m struck by lightning, i can see my reflection in the mirror and the blue lights of the hospital car park, i can feel the cold in the air as it goes in and out of my mouth and my arms flail at it, pushing away at it, until the pain makes me still, and then it is gone.
